quarterly_data.signal: Management leaned on real-world and third-party data to evidence the Wegovy pill launch: 'a recently published study showed that weight loss in the real world exceeded that seen in the OASIS 4 clinical trial at the same point in time.' The U.K. launch was tracked using IQVIA sell-in data to private providers and pharmacies, which showed Novo Nordisk obesity market share rising from around 30% before launch to 45% in July, with around 300,000 patients started in three weeks. Novo now serves more than 46 million people living with obesity and diabetes, with around 1.5 million people on the Wegovy pill worldwide and over 5 million total prescriptions.
quarterly_data.figure: obesity share ~30% to 45% (IQVIA July sell-in); ~300,000 U.K. patients in 3 weeks; 46M people served; 1.5M on Wegovy pill; >5M total prescriptions

quarterly_data.signal: The ZEUS cardiovascular outcomes trial of ziltivekimab, with more than 6,300 people enrolled, failed to reduce MACE with a hazard ratio of 0.99 despite confirmed target engagement and reductions in free IL-6 and hsCRP. Martin Holst Lange framed it as a biomarker-causality test: 'There was a question on the correlation between the biomarkers and the actual outcomes, and that was the leap of faith that had to be tested.' For zenagamtide, an extra titration step was added and management said that 'from a modeling perspective, feel quite confident that we'll see a safety tolerability profile in line with what we've seen with, for example, CagriSema.'
quarterly_data.figure: ZEUS >6,300 patients; MACE hazard ratio 0.99; all-cause mortality hazard ratio 0.99

quarterly_data.signal: Novo invested more than DKK 26 billion into R&D and commercial activities in the quarter, received more than 10 regulatory approvals and started more than 5 clinical trials. The company-wide transformation is running ahead of plan on DKK 8 billion of savings, which are being reinvested into growth opportunities; full-time employees fell to around 66,700, a decrease of almost 12,000 or roughly 15% versus 12 months ago.
quarterly_data.figure: DKK 26B R&D and commercial investment; >10 approvals; >5 trials started; DKK 8B savings; ~66,700 FTEs (-12,000, -15%)

quarterly_data.signal: Second-quarter adjusted sales increased 7% at constant exchange rates to DKK 78.5 billion, driven by GLP-1 volume growth and a favorable prior-period rebate adjustment. Obesity care sales rose 16% and GLP-1 diabetes sales rose 2%; U.S. Operations grew 4% and International Operations grew 10%. Adjusted operating profit increased 11% at constant exchange rates, while adjusted gross margin was 78.2% versus 82.7% a year earlier, including a one-time cost of around DKK 3 billion for right sizing manufacturing capacity agreements.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted sales DKK 78.5B (+7% CER); obesity +16%; GLP-1 diabetes +2%; U.S. +4%; IO +10%; operating profit +11% CER; gross margin 78.2% vs 82.7%

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance was raised again: adjusted sales growth is now expected at 0% to -6% at constant exchange rates and adjusted operating profit growth at 0% to -6%, driven mainly by increased expectations for GLP-1 product sales. The outlook assumes growth in International Operations and decline in U.S. Operations, semaglutide compound patent expiry in certain markets, reduced Medicaid obesity coverage and lower realized prices amplified by most favored nation agreements with the U.S. administration.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted sales growth 0% to -6% CER; adjusted operating profit growth 0% to -6% CER

quarterly_data.signal: Management still expects a U.S. regulatory decision for CagriSema in obesity at the end of 2026 with a potential launch in 2027, and a U.S. regulatory decision for oral semaglutide 25 mg in type 2 diabetes plus U.S. and EU decisions for denecimig in hemophilia A. The ARTEMIS and HERMES cardiovascular outcomes trials of ziltivekimab continue with results expected in the first half of 2027, etavopivat is on track for EU and U.S. submission in Q4 2026, and the company will hold a Capital Markets Day in September.
quarterly_data.figure: CagriSema U.S. decision end-2026, launch 2027; ARTEMIS and HERMES H1 2027; etavopivat submission Q4 2026
